hints.title: Consecutive Pair Seat Swap Logic
hints.text: Exchange the seat numbers of adjacent student pairs (1 with 2, 3 with 4), leaving the last student unchanged if the total count is odd.

hints.title: Case Conditional Identifier Projection
hints.text: For odd identifiers: if equal to max(id), keep id; otherwise increment by 1. For even identifiers: decrement by 1. Order by new id.

hints.title: Seat Exchange Blueprint
hints.text: select case when id % 2 = 1 and id = (select count(*) from Seat) then id when id % 2 = 1 then id + 1 else id - 1 end as id, student from Seat order by id asc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN id % 2 = 1 AND id = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Seat) THEN id
        WHEN id % 2 = 1 THEN id + 1
        ELSE id - 1
    END AS id,
    student
FROM Seat
ORDER BY id ASC;
```

variables: N: number of records in Seat table
complexity.notes: Constant CASE expression computation followed by sorting by exchanged id takes linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full outer self joins create complicated NULL-handling for odd terminal seats.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Mathematical identifier transformation projects new IDs in-place without joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of CASE statement handling the odd trailing seat boundary condition.

import pandas as pd

def exchange_seats(seat: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    n = len(seat)
    df = seat.copy()
    for i in range(0, n - 1, 2):
        temp = df.loc[i, 'student']
        df.loc[i, 'student'] = df.loc[i + 1, 'student']
        df.loc[i + 1, 'student'] = temp
    return df
